_scenario: Urgent case. Ultrasound for gallbladder pain confirms gallstones (answered) and finds a 2.8 cm solid, vascular kidney mass that needs prompt MRI and urology. The UA shows microscopic blood. High-deductible plan with little deductible met, so cost is a real barrier and the Insurance agent matters.

DiagnosticReport.conclusion:
1. Cholelithiasis without sonographic evidence of acute cholecystitis.
2. 2.8 cm solid, vascular exophytic mass in the upper pole of the left kidney, concerning for a renal neoplasm. Recommend contrast-enhanced renal mass protocol MRI or CT.

_sections.title: CLINICAL INDICATION
_sections.text: Intermittent right upper quadrant pain after meals for 3 months. Evaluate for gallstones.

_sections.title: TECHNIQUE
_sections.text: Real-time grayscale and color Doppler sonography of the abdomen.

items.label: Liver
items.text: Normal in size (15.2 cm) and echotexture. No focal lesion. Hepatopetal portal venous flow.

items.label: Gallbladder
items.text: Multiple mobile, shadowing gallstones, the largest measuring 1.4 cm. Wall thickness 2 mm. No pericholecystic fluid. Sonographic Murphy sign is negative.

items.label: Bile ducts
items.text: Common bile duct measures 4 mm. No intrahepatic biliary dilatation.

items.label: Pancreas
items.text: Visualized head and body are unremarkable. The tail is obscured by bowel gas.

items.label: Right kidney
items.text: 10.8 cm. Normal echotexture. No hydronephrosis, stone, or mass.

items.label: Left kidney
items.text: 11.4 cm. 2.8 x 2.5 x 2.6 cm solid, mildly hypoechoic exophytic mass in the upper pole with internal vascularity on color Doppler. No hydronephrosis.
